coverage.notes: Absence claims in this pack describe one search, not the world: a listing of this course's folders in the student's iCloud term archive and his university OneDrive, in September 2026. The course runs on group presentations, each teaching one manufacturing process to the class, followed by a final exam across all the processes. Nearly all of the course material in the archive is other students' work: 14 of the 15 presentation decks were made by other groups. They were deliberately not used for anything, including format evidence. The student's own material is one deck, co-authored with a partner, plus a handwritten outline for it and a personal study guide summarizing every process under the same headings. None of these is an instructor document. There is no syllabus, no presentation prompt, and no rubric, so the requirements (length, required sections, whether economics or a demonstration was expected) are unknown. One deck made to an unknown prompt is not a format.
